- When sentiment turns sharply bullish (↑↑) or bearish (↓↓) in recent days, model tends to overreact — overshoots peak or trough, especially in 30d horizon.
- If sentiment volatility is high (rapid changes) and news volume is low, model often underestimates mean reversion or overcorrects.
- In 30d forecasts, if recent sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) but price is trending down, model often overestimates future price — lagging mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish but price is rising, model tends to underestimate the reversal — underestimates mean reversion or overestimates support.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — underestimates or overestimates direction.
- If sentiment change is negative and price is rising, model tends to overestimate the continuation — ignores sentiment reversal signal.
- In 30d forecasts, if sentiment is bullish but price is falling, model often overestimates the fall — ignores sentiment reversal or misreads momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish and price is rising, model often underestimates the reversal — fails to recognize sentiment shift as a reversal signal.
- If sentiment is bullish and price is falling, model often overestimates the fall — ignores sentiment reversal or misreads momentum.
